name: The five ranks of the real and the apparent (Dongshan / Caoshan)

names.name: zheng pian wuwei 正偏五位 / wuwei junchen 五位君臣

stages.name: zheng zhong pian 正中偏
stages.description: Midnight before the moon shines: meeting without recognising — the real (emptiness, lord) holding the apparent within it.

stages.name: pian zhong zheng 偏中正
stages.description: An old woman who overslept meets an ancient mirror: the real seen within phenomena, no other face than one's own.

stages.name: zheng zhong lai 正中來
stages.description: A road out of nothingness beyond the dust: function arising from the real.

stages.name: jian zhong zhi 兼中至 (also read pian zhong zhi 偏中至)
stages.description: Crossed swords, a lotus in fire: acting freely amid opposites.

stages.name: jian zhong dao 兼中到
stages.description: Not falling into being or non-being; returning to sit among the coals — complete integration.

notes: Bands are an interpretive, low-confidence alignment: Caoshan and the Baojing sanmei present the ranks as relations of lord and minister, real and apparent, not necessarily a sequence; Hakuin's line studies them as a late stage of kōan training. The fourth rank's wording varies between sources.

name: The five ranks of merit (Dongshan)

stages.name: feng 奉
stages.description: Serving the lord — practice in accord.

stages.name: gonggong 共功
stages.description: Merit shared with others / practice and realization together.

notes: Glosses and bands are low-confidence reconstructions; Dongshan answers each with everyday acts rather than definitions.

name: Puming's ten oxherding pictures (the whitening ox)

stages.name: chutiao 初調
stages.description: The nose is pierced; the herder begins training.

stages.name: huishou 回首
stages.description: The ox turns its head back; whitening begins.

stages.name: xiangwang 相忘
stages.description: Herder and ox forget each other; the ox is white.

notes: From memory; titles moderately certain; bands low confidence. Kuoan's series (pth:ten-oxherding-pictures) is owned by U51.

name: The Hakuin-line kōan curriculum

stages.name: shokan (first barrier): mu or the sound of one hand
stages.description: Great doubt on an initial kōan leading to kenshō.

stages.name: goi
stages.description: The Caodong five ranks studied as kōans.

notes: Tradition's account: Hakuin's system. Scholarly account: systematised by his heirs (Tōrei, Gasan, Inzan, Takujū); the named five-fold classification is a later formulation. Low confidence on order and names beyond the first barrier.
